transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-01-15
Start: 14:00 UTC
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Liam O'Connor (Redwood SE), Sanjay Patel (CTO - HelioPharm), Elena Ruiz (Head of Data Privacy), Marcus Lee (ML Engineer), Priya Nair (Product)
Shared artifacts: Redwood security pack (link), retention-config-template.xlsx (link), sample-benchmark-harness.md (link)

[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Maya with Redwood, this is Liam, our solutions engineer. quick intro?
[00:08] Sanjay: Hi, Sanjay here, CTO at HelioPharm. we run clinical trial matching and regulatory summarizations, lots of sensitive patient metadata.
[00:15] Elena: Elena, I'm head of data privacy, want to make sure any PII or PHI is handled per our policies.
[00:20] Marcus: Marcus, ML eng, I'll own the benchmark side.
[00:25] Liam: Great, our agenda is to scope the POC success criteria, discuss data handling (pii, logging, redaction, retention), and agree benchmarks and timeline.

Summary + context
[02:00] Maya: quick background - Redwood supports hosted API, dedicated reserved pools, and private VPC/on-prem installs. For PII we usually offer several levers: prompt-level redaction, disable logging for routes, retention windows, and option to use Private for full customer-controlled storage and KMS.
[02:35] Elena: For us, primary requirement is we cannot persist raw PHI beyond what is necessary for model quality checks. ideally prompts would not be stored, or if stored they need deterministic redaction and encryption with our KMS.
[02:50] Liam: Understood. For the POC we can run two configurations: hosted with logging disabled for the POC routes + automatic redaction pre-ingest, and a private/VPC deployment where data never leaves your network and logs are stored in your S3 behind your KMS.

PII / Redaction specifics
[05:10] Elena: We have a list of PHI fields - names, MRN, dob, addresses. We need to confirm redaction accuracy; false negatives are a no-go.
[05:25] Marcus: what's Redwood's redaction tool? is it regex-based or ML?
[05:30] Liam: We use a hybrid approach - pattern + model-based entity recognition. we provide a redaction policy engine where customers can supply custom patterns. caveat: transcription and NER may be imperfect in audio transcripts; but for text prompts it's higher fidelity.
[06:00] Elena: For the POC we need a measurable redaction accuracy target. I'd like to see >99% recall on our labeled sample.
[06:12] Maya: ok we'll include that as a success criterion for the POC benchmark - test redaction recall on a labeled subset.

Logging, retention, prompt storage
[08:00] Sanjay: Another ask - can we avoid any long-term storage of raw prompts? We prefer ephemeral mode for prompt storage.
[08:12] Liam: There are three modes: 1) Full logging (default for analytics), 2) Redacted logging (store prompts after redaction), 3) Ephemeral/no-logging (don't persist prompt text beyond processing). For hosted we can enable ephemeral/no-logging on a per-route basis for the POC. for auditability, we can store hashes and metrics without text.
[08:45] Elena: Storing hashes is ok as long as the mapping isn't reversible. We also need audit logs for access - who accessed what response.
[09:02] Maya: Redwood's Console provides token-level cost + access logs; audit trails can be exported and forwarded to your SIEM. Access logs do not contain raw prompt text in ephemeral mode.

Encryption and KMS
[10:30] Marcus: If we run dedicated or private, can we integrate with our KMS?
[10:36] Liam: Yes - for Private & Dedicated we support customer-managed keys (AWS KMS/HSM options). For hosted we offer envelope encryption and managed KMS; we can also support Bring-Your-Own-Key for enterprise plans.
[10:50] Sanjay: Good. We'll need the KMS runbook.

Benchmarking: workload sizing and success criteria
[12:00] Liam: For benchmarks we propose: 1k sample queries representative of production traffic, measuring latency P50/P95, throughput (qps) for your typical payload sizes, and redaction recall/precision on labeled data. Success criteria suggestion: P95 latency < 300ms for 512-token requests on dedicated instance; redaction recall >= 99%; end-to-end cost estimate within target.
[12:35] Marcus: Our production mix is short prompts (~120 tokens) for ad-hoc queries and longer clinical summaries (~800 tokens) for batch. we want both covered.
[12:50] Liam: we'll run two benchmark scenarios: interactive (120-token distribution) and summary/batch (800 tokens) to capture both latency and throughput. We'll also test model variant fallbacks - e.g., quantized variant for cost savings.
[13:20] Maya: Also confirm success criteria around quality - what are acceptable regression thresholds for your summarization task?
[13:33] Priya: we want no more than 5% drop in key-phrase recall vs our current baseline.
[13:40] Maya: we'll add that to the benchmark metrics: quality regression threshold <= 5% on your labeled eval set.

Privacy & legal discussion highlights
[15:00] Elena: Legal will want to see data flow diagrams and retention settings. Also SSO, RBAC, and who can see decrypted content.
[15:12] Maya: We'll include a diagram in the security pack + the retention config template. For SSO we support SAML/Okta and granular RBAC.
[15:28] Elena: What about transcript artifacts in Fireflies or other meeting notes?
[15:35] Maya: Those are separate; this POC is scoped for API ingestion only. We'll redact any meeting-level notes if you request.

Operational concerns and logging details
[17:00] Marcus: For the POC harness, can we get an option to stream responses without storing the prompt? Some of our eval tooling expects the text.
[17:10] Liam: You can stream responses to your endpoint; we won't store incoming prompt text if ephemeral mode is enabled. for evaluation you'll need to store outcomes client-side. we can also deliver a secure upload of redacted transcripts if you want centralized evaluation.
[17:35] Marcus: ok that's workable. Also need per-request metadata like request id and routing decisions.
[17:42] Liam: we include request_id, model_version, and route metadata in logs even in ephemeral mode - but again, no prompt text.

Technical edge cases
[20:00] Sanjay: If redaction fails in production, do we have rollback plans? e.g., automatic fallback to private deployment?
[20:12] Liam: Yes - Redwood supports policy-based routing and fallback rules. In the POC we can configure a canary route that if redaction confidence < threshold or if sensitive entity detected, route to your private endpoint or drop storing.
[20:35] Elena: Are there options to run the NER redaction locally before sending to Redwood?
[20:45] Marcus: we were exploring that.
[20:47] Liam: You can pre-process client-side and send already-redacted prompts, then we won't re-store original. we will need to coordinate the schema so we can still compute quality metrics.

Timelines & next steps
[24:00] Maya: Proposed timeline: 1) Week 1 (this week) - exchange security pack and provide PII field list + sample queries. 2) Week 2 - Redwood sets up benchmark harness and runs initial hosted ephemeral tests. 3) Week 3 - run dedicated/private test if needed and evaluate results, review with legal. 4) Week 4 - close POC and decide next stage.
[24:35] Sanjay: Sounds reasonable. Do we have a formal sign-off criteria?
[24:42] Maya: We'll create a short success criteria doc with the items discussed: redaction recall, latency bands per token size, quality regression thresholds, and data handling compliance checks.

Clarifications and small talk
[28:00] Elena: One more thing - retention window. we'd like logs purged after 7 days unless redacted copy is flagged for QA.
[28:12] Liam: Redwood supports configurable retention windows per route; default retention is 30 days but can be set to 0/ephemeral or custom like 7 days. We'll include steps to configure auto-purge and retention policies.
[29:00] Marcus: If we need total string-obliviousness, do you offer an option to only store embeddings and not raw text?
[29:10] Liam: yes you can opt to store only embeddings + metadata; embeddings are irreversible for practical purposes if you don't retain mapping.

Recap & next steps
[35:00] Maya: Quick recap - Action items: we'll send security pack and retention template. Liam will set up benchmark harness; Marcus will provide the sample queries and labeled redaction set; Elena will share the PII list + legal contact. We agreed to run a 1k-query benchmark with both 120-token and 800-token distributions, and redaction recall target >=99%, latency P95 targets as discussed.
[35:40] Elena: We'll also schedule a legal review meeting; please include the data flow diagram.
[35:50] Sanjay: timeline approved.
[36:00] Maya: thanks everyone, we'll follow up with links and a calendar invite for the benchmark kickoff.
[36:12] Priya: thanks, bye.

Notes about transcript quality: auto transcription had typical misspells and sometimes Speaker labels were generic; technical terms like KV cache and quantization were sometimes transcribed oddly (e.g., "K-V cache" vs "KV cache").

End of transcript.
